name: Deflation

subjectOf.text: An artificially scarce currency such as bitcoin is deflationary as long as its market expands, and like gold its price fluctuation makes it unsuitable for daily commerce.
subjectOf.abstract: The artificially scarce bitcoin currency is deflationary as long as its market expands. Like gold, its fluctuation makes it unsuitable for daily commerce.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Eight Institutions for the Evolution of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782205
scope_conditions: holds while the currency's market is expanding

subjectOf.text: Price collapse under AI abundance is structurally different from cyclical deflation: conventional deflation reflects demand contraction or supply shocks inside scarcity frameworks, whereas abundance driven price implosion reflects production possibility frontiers shifting toward infinity.
subjectOf.abstract: Conventional deflation reflects demand contraction or supply shocks within scarcity frameworks. The price "implosion" that AI-driven production generates reflects production possibility frontiers shifting toward infinity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: applies to cognitive and digital goods whose primary inputs become computationally post scarce

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'deflation'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
